<!-- ai-agile/snapshot/v1 by 01_product_docs/prd-writer -->
## Original issue (snapshot before PRD rewrite)

**Original title:** [BUG] - docs - CLAUDE.md must warn that Glob silently misses content behind symlinked directories (standards/, .claude/)

**Original body:**

## Problem statement

Reported live from a consuming-repo session: `Glob("standards/*.json")`
returned nothing even though the files genuinely exist (confirmed via
`Grep` and `ls`/`find` in that session). This caused `prd-writer` on issue
#272 to wrongly conclude "no standards files exist" -- a real,
consequential misdiagnosis, not a cosmetic issue. In that specific case no
correction was needed (nothing in `standards/*.json` actually applied to
that PRD), but the underlying tool gap is real and will misfire on a future
issue where a standard genuinely does apply.

**Independently reproduced and precisely isolated this session**, using a
scratch directory with a real subdirectory and a symlink pointing to it
(mirroring exactly how `standards/` and `.claude/` are installed in every
consuming repo -- see `docs/product/orchestrator/16-onboarding.md`: *"On
Linux/macOS: creates a single directory symlink `standards` -> submodule/standards"*):

- `Glob("standards/*.json")` through the symlink -> **`No files found`**.
- `Glob("real_standards/*.json")` on the real (non-symlinked) directory with
  identical content -> **finds both files correctly.**
- `Grep(path="standards", glob="*.json")` through the same symlink ->
  **finds the files correctly.**
- Plain shell `find standards -name "*.json"` (no `-L`, no trailing slash)
  -> **also returns nothing** -- this is standard, well-known `find`
  behaviour (a symlink given directly as the search root is not descended
  into unless `-L` is passed or the path has a trailing slash). `find -L
  standards -name "*.json"` and `find standards/ -name "*.json"` both work
  correctly.

So the fix isn't simply "use `find` instead of `Glob`" -- a naive `find`
invocation has the exact same trap. The guidance needs to specify the
correct invocation, not just the tool.

This matters specifically because **every consuming repo has `standards/`
and `.claude/` installed as whole-folder symlinks by design** (per
`16-onboarding.md`), so any session working in a consuming repo that uses
`Glob` to check for standards, agents, or commands is exposed to this
silent-empty-result trap on every single check.

### Root cause, precisely located: the real pipeline already prevents this -- the bug is in `/run-agent`

`prd-writer.md`'s frontmatter is `tools: [Bash, Read, Grep]` --
**`Glob` was never in its allowlist.** This isn't advisory: when the
orchestrator spawns `prd-writer` as a real `claude -p` subprocess, it
builds `--allowedTools` from exactly this frontmatter list plus
`pipeline.json`'s per-agent `extra_allowedTools`
(`pipeline_orchestrator.py:2549`), plus `--disallowedTools "Task,Agent,Skill"`
(`:2555`). In a genuine orchestrator-driven run, `prd-writer` **cannot call
`Glob` at all** -- the tool is structurally absent from that subprocess.

So the reported bug should not be reproducible through the real pipeline.
The mechanism that *would* have prevented it already exists and is already
correctly configured. The actual gap: **`.claude/commands/run-agent.md`
(the driver that runs an agent's `.md` file inline inside the current
interactive session, "you see each step live") never constructs an
`--allowedTools` restriction at all.** It doesn't spawn a subprocess, so
there is nothing to pass the flag to -- the session simply keeps whatever
tools it already had (which, like most interactive sessions, includes
`Glob`), regardless of what the target agent's frontmatter declares. This
is almost certainly where the client-repo session actually hit this: not a
real orchestrator run of `prd-writer`, but an interactive run (via
`/run-agent` or an equivalent inline execution) where the tool-scoping
enforcement the real pipeline relies on simply doesn't apply.

This is the same shape of gap as
[#305](https://github.com/M-A-Operating-System/ai-coding-standards2/issues/305)
(headless-vs-interactive execution-mode spike) -- interactive execution
silently skipping a constraint the real orchestrator enforces.

## Goal

`.claude/CLAUDE.md` (the framework-owned file symlinked into every
consuming repo, already the vehicle for two similar "verify before
trusting a tool" additions this session) instructs sessions to use `Grep`
or `find -L` / `find {path}/` -- not `Glob` -- when checking for content
under `standards/` or `.claude/`, and explains why: `Glob` does not follow
a symlinked directory and returns an empty result silently, with no error
to signal the miss.

## Proposed approach (decide in design)

Two fixes, complementary rather than either/or -- the first catches this
symptom specifically and applies regardless of execution mode; the second
closes the actual mechanism gap that let it happen and would prevent this
whole *class* of drift, not just this one tool:

**1. Doc-level (catches the general case, any session, any context):**
- Add a bullet to `.claude/CLAUDE.md` -- Section 1 ("Think Before Coding")
  is the natural fit alongside the existing "a tool/API failure in one
  context is not evidence of a platform-wide restriction" bullet, since
  this is the same class of lesson (a tool's silent-empty result isn't
  proof of absence; verify with a different tool before concluding).
- State the concrete, correct alternative precisely enough that a session
  doesn't reach for a naive `find standards -name "*.json"` and hit the
  same trap: use `Grep` (which handles this correctly, confirmed above),
  or `find -L {path}` / `find {path}/` (trailing slash) if a raw file
  listing is needed.
- Name `standards/` and `.claude/` explicitly as the two paths this
  concretely affects in every consuming repo, since those are the
  whole-folder symlinks this framework itself installs.

**2. Mechanism-level (the stronger fix -- closes the enforcement gap
itself):** `run-agent.md` should read the target agent's `tools:`
frontmatter and `pipeline.json` `extra_allowedTools`, and actually
constrain the interactive session to that set (or, if a hard runtime
restriction isn't feasible for an inline/non-subprocess execution, at
minimum warn explicitly before the session uses a tool outside that
declared allowlist). This would make `/run-agent` match the real
pipeline's tool-scoping for *every* agent and *every* tool, not just
`prd-writer` and `Glob` -- the `Glob`/symlink case is a symptom of a
general gap, not the whole problem.

## Acceptance criteria (Gherkin)

#### Scenario: A session checking standards content is warned about the symlink trap
**Given** `.claude/CLAUDE.md` after this change
**When** a session is about to check `standards/*.json` (or any path under `.claude/`) for content
**Then** the doc instructs using `Grep` or a symlink-following `find` invocation instead of `Glob`, and explains that `Glob` can silently return an empty result through a symlinked directory

#### Scenario: The guidance specifies a correct invocation, not just a tool name
**Given** the same doc
**When** a reader looks for the recommended alternative
**Then** it names a concrete, verified-correct invocation (`Grep`, or `find -L` / a trailing-slash `find`) rather than just "use find," which would not by itself avoid the same trap

#### Scenario: The affected paths are named explicitly
**Given** the same doc
**When** a reader wants to know which paths this actually affects
**Then** `standards/` and `.claude/` are named as the whole-folder symlinks every consuming repo installs, per `16-onboarding.md`

#### Scenario: An interactively-run agent is scoped to its declared tool allowlist
**Given** `/run-agent` invoked on an agent whose frontmatter declares `tools: [Bash, Read, Grep]` (no `Glob`)
**When** the interactive session follows that agent's instructions
**Then** it is constrained to (or explicitly warned before stepping outside) the same tool set the real orchestrator-spawned subprocess would have -- `Glob` is not silently available just because the ambient session happens to have it

## References

- Live report: consuming-repo session, issue #272, `prd-writer` wrongly concluding no standards files exist due to `Glob("standards/*.json")` returning empty.
- Reproduced and isolated this session: `Glob` vs `Grep` vs `find` (with and without `-L`/trailing slash) against an identical symlink setup -- see conversation for the exact commands and outputs.
- `docs/product/orchestrator/16-onboarding.md` -- documents `standards/` and `.claude/` as whole-folder symlinks (`standards -> submodule/standards`, `.claude -> submodule/.claude`) installed in every consuming repo.
- `.claude/CLAUDE.md` Section 1 ("Think Before Coding") -- the existing "verify a tool/API result before generalizing" bullet this pairs with; same file, same class of lesson.
- `.claude/agents/01_product_docs/prd-writer.md:13` -- `tools: [Bash, Read, Grep]`, confirming `Glob` was never in `prd-writer`'s allowlist.
- `pipeline/pipeline_orchestrator.py:2549,2555` -- `--allowedTools`/`--disallowedTools` construction from frontmatter + `extra_allowedTools`, the real enforcement mechanism this issue's root-cause analysis traces.
- `.claude/commands/run-agent.md` -- the interactive driver that does not construct any equivalent restriction, the actual gap that let this manifest.
- [#305](https://github.com/M-A-Operating-System/ai-coding-standards2/issues/305) -- same class of gap (interactive execution skipping a constraint the real orchestrator enforces), different mechanism.

## Notes / out of scope

- Not proposing a change to the `Glob` tool's own behaviour -- this is
  scoped to documenting the trap so sessions route around it, not fixing
  the tool itself.
- Not auditing every existing agent prompt (`prd-writer.md`,
  `pr-reviewer.md`, etc.) for `Glob`-against-`standards/` usage in this
  issue -- that's a reasonable follow-up once this guidance lands, not
  bundled here.
- The mechanism-level fix (`run-agent.md` tool-scoping enforcement) is
  proposed here because this bug is the concrete evidence for it, but the
  actual design of *how* an inline, non-subprocess interactive session
  enforces a tool restriction (hard block vs. warn-before-use) is a real
  open question for design, not resolved by this issue.
